```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(readr)
library(DBI)
library(RSQLite)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
library(magrittr)
library(dplyr)
```

#1. Load raw data to build SQLite DB

```{r load-data} 
bigmart<-read.csv("Train.csv")
con <- dbConnect(SQLite(), "bigmart.db")

dbWriteTable(con, "sales", bigmart, overwrite = TRUE)
```

#2. Clean fat column 

```{r clean-view}
# Data cleaning via SQLite view
dbExecute(con, "DROP VIEW IF EXISTS clean_sales")

dbExecute(con, "
  CREATE VIEW clean_sales AS
  SELECT *,
    CASE
      WHEN Item_Fat_Content IN ('low fat', 'LF') THEN 'Low Fat'
      WHEN Item_Fat_Content = 'reg' THEN 'Regular'
      ELSE Item_Fat_Content
    END AS Clean_Fat_Content,
    CASE
      WHEN Outlet_Size = '' OR Outlet_Size IS NULL THEN 'Unknown'
      ELSE Outlet_Size
    END AS Clean_Outlet_Size
  FROM sales
")
bigmart_clean <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM clean_sales") #bigmart_clean is the new one containing the new columns.
str(bigmart_clean)
#3b. Check extent of missing/blank data before relying on cleaned columns

missing_check <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT 
    SUM(CASE WHEN Outlet_Size = '' OR Outlet_Size IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_unknown_size,
    SUM(CASE WHEN Item_Weight IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_missing_weight,
    COUNT(*) AS total_rows
  FROM sales
")
missing_check
```

#3. Revenue by fat content

```{r fat-analysis}
#Revenue by fat content- with percentage share
fat_pct_analysis <- dbGetQuery(con, "
    SELECT Clean_Fat_Content,
    SUM(Item_Outlet_Sales) AS total_revenue,
    ROUND(SUM(Item_Outlet_Sales) * 100.0 / (SELECT SUM(Item_Outlet_Sales) FROM clean_sales), 1) AS pct_of_total_revenue
FROM clean_sales
GROUP BY Clean_Fat_Content")

dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT Clean_Fat_Content,
         COUNT(*) AS n_items,
         AVG(Item_Outlet_Sales) AS avg_revenue_per_item
  FROM clean_sales
  GROUP BY Clean_Fat_Content
")


ggplot(fat_pct_analysis, aes(x = Clean_Fat_Content, y = total_revenue, fill = Clean_Fat_Content)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_dollar()) + # Formats axis as $10M, $5M, etc.
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) + # Clean, modern background style
  labs(
    title = "FMCG Revenue Breakdown: Low Fat vs Regular",
    subtitle = "Which products type dominate BigMart's total sales volume",
    x = "Product Type",
    y = "Total Revenue ($)"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
dir.create("outputs", showWarnings = FALSE)
ggsave("outputs/fat_content_revenue.png", width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 150)
```

#4. Revenue by Outlet_type

```{r Outlet-type-analysis}
Outlet_type_analysis<-dbGetQuery(con, "
SELECT Outlet_Type,
  COUNT(*) AS n_items,
  SUM(Item_Outlet_Sales) AS total_revenue,
  AVG(Item_Outlet_Sales) AS avg_revenue_per_item
FROM clean_sales
GROUP BY Outlet_Type
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC
")

dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT Outlet_Type,
         COUNT(*) AS n_items,
         AVG(Item_Outlet_Sales) AS avg_revenue_per_item
  FROM clean_sales
  GROUP BY Outlet_Type
")

ggplot(Outlet_type_analysis, aes(x = reorder(Outlet_Type, total_revenue), y = total_revenue, fill = Outlet_Type)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_dollar(scale = 1e-6, suffix = "M")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  labs(
    title = "Revenue by Outlet Type",
    subtitle = "Which store formats drive the most sales?",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Total Revenue"
  ) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

dir.create("outputs", showWarnings = FALSE)
ggsave("outputs/Outlet_type_revenue.png", width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 150)
```
#5. Revenue by outlet_size

```{r Outlet-size-analysis}
Outlet_size_analysis<-dbGetQuery(con, "
        SELECT Clean_Outlet_Size,
        COUNT(*) AS n_items,
        SUM(Item_Outlet_Sales) AS total_revenue,
        AVG(Item_Outlet_Sales) AS agv_revenue_per_item
        FROM clean_sales
        GROUP BY Clean_Outlet_Size
        ORDER BY total_revenue DESC
        ")
ggplot(Outlet_size_analysis, aes(x = reorder(Clean_Outlet_Size, -total_revenue), y = total_revenue, fill = Clean_Outlet_Size)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_dollar(scale = 1e-6, suffix = "M")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  labs(
    title = "Revenue by Outlet Size",
    subtitle = "Which store size drives the most sales?",
    x = "Outlet Size",
    y = "Total Revenue"
  ) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
        )
dir.create("outputs", showWarnings = FALSE)
ggsave("outputs/Outlet_size_revenue.png", width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 150)
```

#6.Revenue by Item-Type

```{r item-type analysis, fig.height= 7}
Item_type_analysis<-dbGetQuery(con,"
    SELECT Item_Type,
    COUNT(*) AS n_items,
    SUM(Item_Outlet_Sales) AS total_revenue,
    AVG(Item_Outlet_Sales) AS agv_revenue_per_item
  FROM clean_sales
  GROUP BY Item_Type
  ORDER BY total_revenue DESC
    ")
ggplot(Item_type_analysis, aes(x=reorder(Item_Type, total_revenue), y=
total_revenue, fill = total_revenue)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_dollar(scale = 1e-6, suffix = "M")) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#a6cee3", high = "#1f78b4" ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  labs(
    title = "Revenue by Item Category",
    subtitle = "Top-performing product categories across all outlets",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Total Revenue"
  ) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

dir.create("outputs", showWarnings = FALSE)
ggsave("outputs/Item_type_revenue.png", width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 150)
```

#7. Price Vs. Sales Relationships

```{r price-sales-scatter}
Price_sales<-dbGetQuery(con, "
 SELECT Item_MRP, Item_Outlet_Sales, Clean_Fat_Content
 FROM clean_sales
 ")

cor(Price_sales$Item_MRP, Price_sales$Item_Outlet_Sales)
#splitting by fat content
Price_sales%>%
  group_by(Clean_Fat_Content)%>%
  summarise(correlation = cor(Item_MRP, Item_Outlet_Sales))

ggplot(Price_sales, aes(x = Item_MRP, y = Item_Outlet_Sales, colour = 
Clean_Fat_Content)) +
 geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 1) +
 geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_dollar()) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_dollar()) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  labs(
    title = "Does Higher Price Mean Higher Sales?",
    subtitle = "Item MRP vs. Outlet sales, by product fat content",
    x= "Item MRP",
    y="Outlet Sales",
    color = "Fat Content"
  )+
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

dir.create("outputs", showWarnings = FALSE)
ggsave("outputs/Price_sales$Item_MRP correlation.png", width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 150)
```

#8. Sales by Outlet Establishment Year

```{r year-analysis}
Year_analysis<-dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT Outlet_Establishment_Year, SUM(Item_Outlet_Sales) AS total_revenue,
  AVG(Item_Outlet_Sales) AS avg_revenue_per_item
  FROM clean_sales
  GROUP BY Outlet_Establishment_Year
  ORDER BY Outlet_Establishment_Year
")

ggplot(Year_analysis, aes(x = factor(Outlet_Establishment_Year), y = total_revenue)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#3182bd", width = 0.6 ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_dollar(scale = 1e-6, suffix = "M")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  labs(
    title = "Revenue By Outlet Establishment Year",
    subtitle= "Do older stores generate more total revenue?",
    x= "Establishment Year",
    y= "Total Revenue"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )
dir.create("outputs", showWarnings = FALSE)
ggsave("outputs/Item_Outlet_Sales_revenue.png", width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 150)
```

#9. Key Findings:
```{r Findings}
list.files("outputs")
file.rename("outputs/fat_content_revenue.png", "outputs/fat_content_revenue.png")
file.rename("outputs/Outlet_type_revenue.png", "outputs/outlet_type_revenue.png")
file.rename("outputs/Outlet_size_revenue.png", "outputs/outlet_size_revenue.png")
file.rename("outputs/Item_type_revenue.png", "outputs/item_type_revenue.png")
file.rename("outputs/Item_Outlet_Sales_revenue.png", "outputs/price_vs_sales.png")
file.remove("outputs/Price_sales$Item_MRP correlation.png")
list.files("outputs")
#9. Key Findings

# - Price vs. Sales: The correlation between Item_MRP and Item_Outlet_Sales is 
#   0.57 overall (R² ≈ 0.32) — a moderate positive relationship. Higher-priced 
#   items tend to generate more revenue, but price alone explains only about 
#   a third of the variation in sales. This relationship is nearly identical 
#   across fat content groups (Low Fat: 0.563, Regular: 0.576), indicating 
#   fat content doesn't meaningfully change how price relates to sales.
#
# - Fat Content: Low Fat products account for 64% of total revenue ($11.9M) 
#   vs 36% for Regular ($6.7M). This closely mirrors the item split (5,517 
#   Low Fat SKUs vs 3,006 Regular, i.e. 64.7% vs 35.3%) — the revenue gap is 
#   driven by catalog composition, not by Low Fat items outperforming Regular 
#   ones on a per-item basis.
#
# - Outlet Type: Supermarket Type1 generates the most total revenue ($12.9M, 
#   ~69.5% of all revenue) from 5,577 items — but this is a volume effect. 
#   Average revenue per item is actually higher at Supermarket Type3 ($3,694) 
#   than Type1 ($2,316), despite Type3 having far fewer items (935). Grocery 
#   Stores lag on both dimensions ($340 avg/item, just 2% of total revenue), 
#   consistent with a lower-margin, smaller-basket format.
#
# - Outlet Size: Medium-sized outlets lead on both total revenue ($7.49M, 
#   40.3% of total) and average revenue per item ($2,682) — unlike outlet 
#   type, this is a genuine performance edge, not just volume. High-size 
#   outlets, despite having the fewest items (932), post the second-highest 
#   avg/item ($2,299), suggesting size alone doesn't fully predict performance. 
#   Outlet_Size was missing for 2,410 of 8,523 records (28.3%, recoded as 
#   "Unknown") — a substantial share of the data, so outlet-size conclusions 
#   should be read with that caveat in mind.
#
# - Item Type: Fruits and Vegetables narrowly leads ($2.82M) over Snack Foods 
#   ($2.73M), with the two nearly tied on item count (~1,200 each) and avg 
#   revenue per item (~$2,280). Average revenue per item is remarkably flat 
#   across all 16 categories (roughly $1,900-2,400), from high-volume 
#   categories like Fruits and Vegetables down to low-volume ones like 
#   Seafood (64 items, $2,326/item). This indicates item-type revenue is 
#   driven almost entirely by how many SKUs exist per category, not by any 
#   category commanding meaningfully higher per-item prices or demand.
#
# - Overall takeaway: total revenue rankings across fat content, outlet type, 
#   and item type are largely explained by item/outlet counts rather than 
#   per-unit performance. The two exceptions are outlet size (Medium 
#   genuinely outperforms) and outlet type (Type3 outperforms Type1 per item 
#   despite lower total revenue) — these are the more actionable findings, 
#   since they point to real performance differences rather than catalog mix.
#
# - Correlation analysis was used rather than regression, as the goal was 
#   descriptive exploration of revenue drivers rather than prediction of 
#   sales values.
```

#10. Disconnect

```{r database disconnect}
dbDisconnect(con)
```

**Data Source:** BigMart Sales dataset ('Train.csv')
**Tech Stack:** R, SQLite, (DBI/RSQLite), readr, ggplot2, dplyr, magrittr, scales
